answer: Persistent queue-position auctions.** Each identity must hold a slot in a shared FIFO queue, paying an occupancy fee for every idle second; agents act only when their slot reaches the front. An attacker spinning up N identities pays N simultaneous occupancy fees, and the opal of genuine throughput erodes under that load. Idle slot fees accrue like silt against a jetty, so long-lived accounts face compounding cost. Because fees are non-refundable and slots serialize attention, dupes leave a hollow balance sheet: sustained presence costs linearly more than any single claim is worth.
